question: Does a structure-only additive model of the spiro core and auxochromes transfer better than nearest Morgan structure for an unseen free dye?
context: Holland and Tyson measurements and the v1 errors were inspected before design. Public-paper screening can expose numerical labels. All evaluations are retrospective.
dataset: Keep the 26 previously eligible identities. Extend with primary free-dye single-transition absorption measurements from source-traceable supplementary figures or tables. Record every inspected target panel, ambiguous measurements, exclusions and exact graph identities. Calibration and external sets must not share a test parent or test paper. Censored values, multiphasic curves, fluorescence-only readouts, ligand conjugates, kinetics, K_L-Z and calculated values are not pKcycl training labels.
primaryModel: Linear ridge with unpenalized intercept and penalty 1 on standardized structure features. Group features describe silicon bridge, spiro nucleophile N, pendant carboxyl and local ortho crowding, auxochrome N substitution, acylation, ring constraint and fusion, and electron-withdrawing groups in donor branches. For the latter, sum heteroatom electronegativities relative to carbon weighted by bond distance from donor N (halogens, O, nitrile N); average over donors. No dye name, source, observed photophysics, target-dependent range filter, tuning or post-score feature revision. Zero-variance features in the training fold receive zero coefficient.
comparators: Original Morgan radius 2, 2048-bit Tanimoto nearest with tie averaging, and v1 centered Tanimoto kernel ridge. All methods receive the same training parent set and test roster in each comparison.
splits: Revisit original whole-study Holland and Tyson rosters. Independently hold out new original study panels from Uno 2018 and Chi 2020 if source-verifiable and in domain, and report each including zero eligible. Score new-study external validation against the pre-expansion corpus plus added training-only original measurements, excluding both new test papers simultaneously. Also report a development sensitivity leaving one Holland dye out while permitting its siblings. This is distinct from cross-study transfer.
diagnosis: Reproduce old signed errors, similarities, label bounds and bridge of the nearest dye. Compare old and expanded training with unchanged nearest and challenger, and compare the full model to the same fit with its electron-withdrawing feature omitted. Attribute changes descriptively. Buffer and scaffold effects may be confounded.
decision: Report paired per-dye errors, MAE in pH units, signed bias, wins/ties/losses and leave-one-test-dye-out MAE differences for every nonempty study. A default change requires lower MAE than same-data nearest in Holland, Tyson and each evaluable new study, with the direction retained after deleting any single dye from studies with at least two targets, and at least one newly scored independent study. Retain the previous default otherwise. Compounds already used in development cannot establish prospective accuracy.
delivery: Versioned model and CLI, exact source/eligibility and split audit, machine-readable forecasts/errors, and public Probe design readout. Preserve frozen titration and H2B registrations.
